edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults with recurrent depression in remission
edges.mechanism: Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy helps relapse prevention by making recurrent negative thought patterns easier to notice before they become full depressive episodes.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2018 Shallcross rct in Behav Ther already points to mindfulness-based cognitive therapy tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
